clue.text: Being intransigent and shaking heads, demonstrating partiality

indicators.note: the heads of the four words before it are their first letters, so each word gives only its initial

explanation.surface: A stubborn person shaking their head shows they favour one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking heads' reads as a gesture, but 'heads' takes the first letters of Being, intransigent, and, shaking; 'demonstrating' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a prejudice towards one side, which is exactly what partiality means.

clue.text: Protesting hotly as half of us apply bear hug

indicators.note: a two-letter word cut in half leaves just its first letter here

parts.note: a bear hug pins the other person's arms to their sides

explanation.surface: Half of us angrily object while someone squeezes us in a bear hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes U, the first half of 'us'; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angrily indignant, protesting with heat.

clue.text: Too content for meals-on-wheels

indicators.note: the contents of the hyphenated phrase are the letters held inside it, so the answer sits within it

explanation.surface: Something that is also included among the food delivered by a meals-on-wheels service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like a noun about food, but 'content for' points to the run inside meALS-On-wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms, both meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Mass of lymphatic tissue giving don ideas

indicators.note: giving here means yielding something new, the letters of the two words remade into another word

explanation.surface: Some tissue in the throat supposedly inspiring a university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' rearranges DON IDEAS; a don is a British university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are a mass of lymphoid tissue at the back of the nose, part of the lymphatic system.

clue.text: Burial mound in Furness

definitions.meaning: a prehistoric earthwork raised over a grave is called a ...
completes the name of ...-in-Furness, a shipbuilding town in Cumbria, north-west England

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as a location for the mound, but it is the tail of a place name: Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is an ancient grave mound, and Barrow is the town's short name.

clue.text: It may be trained in bad Rowling novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters before it take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Something gets trained in a poor book by the author of Harry Potter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by J. K. Rowling but is the anagram signal for BAD ROWLING; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding dress often has a train, a long trailing back panel, so it may be described as trained.

clue.text: Gangster eliminating Fanny Adams is hard to find

indicators.note: eliminating means getting rid of, so one piece is taken out of the gangster's name

parts.note: Scarface was the nickname of the Chicago gangster Al Capone
sweet Fanny Adams, British slang for nothing at all, is abbreviated FA

explanation.surface: A mobster who has disposed of a woman named Fanny Adams is now elusive.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny Adams reads as a victim, but 'sweet FA' is British slang for nothing; 'eliminating' removes FA from SCARFACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, so it is difficult to come by.

clue.text: Like extremely poisonous snakes

parts.note: like and as both mean in the manner of

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A remark about some snakes being highly venomous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'poisonous' but takes its outer letters, P and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, such as the Egyptian cobra of Cleopatra's legend.

clue.text: Drive one mile and move rapidly, being short of time

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to pelt is to run or move very fast

explanation.surface: A driver goes a mile at speed despite running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being short of time' sounds like hurry, but it drops T from PELT, leaving PEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push something forward.

clue.text: Acceleration tests Doctor Arnold first introduced with Thalia and her sisters

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the name it follows

parts.note: Thalia is one of the three Graces of Greek myth, with Aglaia and Euphrosyne

explanation.surface: A doctor named Arnold meeting the three goddesses of charm and beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: Thalia is also one of the Muses, which may lead you astray, but here she is one of the three Graces; 'introduced with' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag races are short sprints between cars from a standing start, testing acceleration.

clue.text: Drink with Pole and German proprietor

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the South Pole
und is German for and
a proprietor is an owner

explanation.surface: A Polish man and a German businessman sharing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish man but is a geographic pole; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an evening alcoholic drink taken around sunset.

clue.text: Girl in mainland or island area of Greece

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the words that follow, spanning them

parts.words: mainland or island area of Greece

explanation.surface: A young woman found somewhere in Greece, whether on the mainland or an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in mainlanD OR ISland; Doris was also an area of ancient Greece, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris is a woman's first name, so it fits a clue asking for a girl.

clue.text: Temptress learning flower arrangement in Hawaii

parts.note: lore is accumulated knowledge or learning
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A seductress picking up the craft of floristry in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower arrangement' suggests an anagram, but it is the Hawaiian garland, LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a siren of German legend who lured Rhine boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Sign in more than 50% of reading rooms

indicators.note: just over half of the nine-letter word is kept, its first five letters, the tail being dropped

parts.note: libraries are rooms for reading

explanation.surface: A notice found in most library reading rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Five letters of LIBRARIES is just over half; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: What cobblers need — part of shoe that was depicted by Leonardo

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped form a cobbler builds a shoe on
the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole

explanation.surface: A shoemaking aside that turns suddenly into art history.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobblers' talk hides Leonardo da Vinci's mural of Christ's final meal with the apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci painted the famous mural of Christ's final meal with his disciples in Milan.

clue.text: German leader is going to mass — he's impressed

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: will expresses the future, like is going to
the pronoun he, with the 's read as is
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A German leader attending Mass and coming away moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' reads as admiration at Mass, but it signals one piece pressed inside another; 'going to' is the future sense of will.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm II was the last German Kaiser, so a German leader of that name fits.

clue.text: Extra-large mushroom

parts.note: extra and more both mean additional
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A description of a huge fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra-large' reads as one size label but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The morel is an edible fungus with a honeycombed cap.

clue.text: Foundation and front of building unchanged

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: as is means left as it stands, unaltered

explanation.surface: A building's foundations and facade left untouched by renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word; 'front of' takes B from building.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the underlying support on which something rests.

clue.text: Smart card for Alastair

definitions.meaning: a chip card in a mobile phone that identifies the subscriber
the Scottish actor Alastair ..., famous in British comedy films

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; Alastair Sim was a much-loved Scottish film actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A SIM card is a smart card for phones, and Sim is the actor's surname.

clue.text: Unfinished look in state publication

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Maine is a state of the USA

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is missing

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

explanation.surface: A partial glance at an official state publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the E of GAZE to give GAZ, which goes 'in' MAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is a periodical publication.

clue.text: Speaker's call (not loud) for socialist revolution

indicators.note: not means without, so one letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A call, not shouted, for a socialist uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not loud)' removes F from 'for' to give OR; 'revolution' turns RED to DER. The Speaker chairs the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker of the House of Commons calls out the word to restore discipline in debate.

clue.text: Barrie's family favourites

definitions.meaning: in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan, Wendy, John and Michael belong to the Darling family
loved ones or pets are called ...

explanation.walkthrough: J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan; the children Wendy, John and Michael are Darlings.
explanation.definitionFit: The family in Peter Pan are the Darlings, and darlings also means favourites or loved ones.

clue.text: Essayist is framed by accessory

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the first word goes inside the second

parts.note: an add-on is an extra or accessory

explanation.surface: A writer finds himself set up by an accomplice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accessory' suggests a criminal accomplice, but here it is an add-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an English essayist who co-founded The Spectator.

clue.text: Work in yard, twisting left foot

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
twisting turns the abbreviation round

parts.note: an act is a deed or piece of work

explanation.surface: Doing some work in the garden and twisting a left foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' turns YD into DY; ACT goes 'in' it. 'foot' is the metrical unit, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A dactyl is a metrical foot of one stressed syllable followed by two unstressed.

clue.text: Arrest Latin American in Palestinian city

parts.note: to nab is to arrest

explanation.surface: A Latin American being detained in a city in Palestine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin American' reads as one person but is two pieces; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nablus is a city in the West Bank, Palestine.

clue.text: Universal soldier?

definitions.meaning: applying to all, common to everyone
a senior military officer of high rank; the question mark flags the understatement

explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the song and film title 'Universal Soldier'.
explanation.definitionFit: General means widespread or universal, and a general is an army officer.

clue.text: Democrat leaves MP to sum up

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so a letter goes out of the word

parts.note: in Britain a redcap is a military policeman, from their red caps

explanation.surface: A Democrat quits Parliament to give a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like a Member of Parliament but is Military Police, known as REDCAPs in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise, short for recapitulate.

clue.text: Free and easy start for journey

parts.note: to rid is to free from something

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An easy, carefree beginning to a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free and easy' reads as a phrase but splits; 'and' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a journey on a vehicle or animal.

clue.text: Carmen's last appearance in any Bizet production is too complicated

indicators.note: a production makes something new, so the letters are reworked
last takes the final letter of the possessive name

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The final appearance of Carmen in any staging of Bizet's opera is overcomplicated.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last letter of Carmen, joins ANY BIZET and 'production' rearranges them; 'appearance in' and 'is' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Byzantine describes something excessively intricate, like the bureaucracy of the Byzantine Empire.

clue.text: Straight man's last to scoff

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the word

parts.note: to scoff is British slang for eating greedily

explanation.surface: A heterosexual man's final act is to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; 'scoff' means eat greedily in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat describes a spirit drunk straight, without water or mixer.

clue.text: Bring in vessel in sound

indicators.note: in sound means as heard spoken, so the word is matched by how it is said

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Bringing a ship into a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship and 'sound' a sea channel, but URN said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to bring in money as income.

clue.text: Train ready? Go for ticket

indicators.note: to train is to shape or direct, so the following letters are reshaped

parts.note: a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Is the train ready? Go and buy a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway noun but is the anagram signal on READY, giving DAYRE; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A day return is a British rail ticket for travel out and back on the same day.

clue.text: A much bigger 'and tool?

parts.note: huger, said Cockney-fashion with the initial H dropped, as the apostrophe in 'and shows

explanation.surface: A Cockney asking about a much bigger hand tool.
explanation.walkthrough: ''and' is 'hand' with the H dropped, Cockney style, which signals HUGER losing its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a hand tool for boring holes in wood.
